claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
A VEC-guided rapid composition-screening approach has been used in arc-melted Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloys.
Ta and V enrichment together with Mo and W depletion was beneficial in Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W alloys.
VEC-guided composition screening with experimental calibration can predict Young's modulus for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
VEC-guided composition screening with experimental calibration can predict yield strength for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
VEC-guided composition screening with experimental calibration can predict fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
Maintaining similar thermal processing will preserve the alloy's hierarchical microstructure during testing.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates the effect of composition changes on bonding characteristics.
The hierarchical heterostructure mediates the effect of composition changes on phase distributions.
Changes in bonding characteristics and phase distributions affect mechanical performance.
Targeted compositional adjustments alter the alloy's valence electron concentration.
Altered valence electron concentration modulates bonding and phase behavior within the hierarchical structure.
Experimentally calibrated empirical correlations reduce computational demands by replacing complex simulations.
The proposed method will predict the three mechanical properties to approximately within ±10% of measured values.
The proposed method will reduce time-to-result by approximately a factor of three relative to conventional computation-intensive methods.
The proposed method will improve fracture-toughness prediction over previous methods.
Combined full-scale CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and complex machine-learning models are computationally heavy and inefficient.
Conventional approaches are especially limited in predicting fracture toughness.
Disruption of the hierarchical heterostructure by excessive annealing or phase separation would invalidate the VEC-based correlations.

contradictions.description: The stated base alloy HfNbTiVAl10 contains neither Mo nor W, yet the proposed modification and benchmark call for Mo/W depletion. Ta enrichment would also change the stated alloy system, but no substitution rule or revised composition is provided.

The predictions are framed for HfNbTiVAl10 in its reported hierarchical state, whereas the benchmark tests compositionally modified samples. The design does not establish that these modified samples remain the same nominal alloy or reproduce the reported hierarchical state.
